facts.fact_text: On 10 April 2006 a group of seven people living in the Dokuzparinskiy District of Dagestan posted a written notice informing the district authorities that on 25 April 2006 they would hold a public demonstration in the village of Usukhchay.
The Dokuzparinskiy District of Dagestan is a mountainous region close to the border with Azerbaijan.
The applicants' names were not mentioned in the list of organisers of the demonstration planned for 25 April 2006 in the village of Usukhchay.
One of the principal aims of the demonstration planned for 25 April 2006 in the village of Usukhchay was to criticise the work of the head of the local administration, Mr A.
One of the principal aims of the demonstration planned for 25 April 2006 in the village of Usukhchay was to denounce corruption and the misuse of public funds by the local administration.

One of the principal aims of the demonstration planned for 25 April 2006 in the village of Usukhchay was to draw attention to the inactivity of the law-enforcement agencies regarding abuses committed by Mr A. and his colleagues.
The demonstration planned for 25 April 2006 was supposed to be held in a recreational park in the village of Usukhchay from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m.
The estimated number of participants in the demonstration planned for 25 April 2006 in the village of Usukhchay was 5,000.
The organisers of the demonstration planned for 25 April 2006 in the village of Usukhchay asked the police to dispatch officers for the protection of those participating in the demonstration.

Although the applicants' names were not in the notice of the demonstration planned for 25 April 2006 in the village of Usukhchay, the applicants claimed that they had played an active part in the organisation of the meeting in their respective communities.

The notice of the demonstration planned for 25 April 2006 in the village of Usukhchay was sent to the district administration with copies to the Dokuzparinskiy district prosecutor and the head of the district police department.
The applicants produced a copy of a payment slip from a post office in Makhachkala indicating that the notice of the demonstration had been posted by registered mail on 10 April 2006.

According to the final report of the internal inquiry of 10 May 2006, at 4.45 p.m. on 25 April 2006 Colonel Iz. had ordered his officers to unblock the road near Miskindzha, but the officers were attacked by a group of men armed with iron rods, stones and knives.
According to the final report of the internal inquiry of 10 May 2006, some of the men who attacked the police near Miskindzha on 25 April 2006 tried to grab the officers' service guns.
According to the final report of the internal inquiry of 10 May 2006, when the police entered Miskindzha on 25 April 2006, they discovered a lorry loaded with alcohol, cigarettes and foodstuff.
Lieutenant-Colonel Mr Og. testified that his men had been fired at from the nearby gardens located on the left side of the road near Miskindzha on 25 April 2006.
Police officer Mr Il. (who had sustained a bullet wound to his thigh) testified that a hooded man had shot at him with a hunter's gun during the events of 25 April 2006 near Miskindzha.
An appendix to the internal inquiry of 10 May 2006 described restrictions on the use of gas grenades; in particular, it was prohibited to "shoot gas grenades directly at humans".

On 19 October 2006 the Regional Prosecutor's Office of the Dagestan Republic opened a criminal investigation under Article 286 § 3 (b) and (c) of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation ("Abuse of office") concerning the killing of Mr Ng. (case no. 668459).
On 4 December 2006 criminal cases nos. 668459 and 67611 were joined.
According to the Government, within criminal cases nos. 668459 and 67611 the investigators questioned more than seventy witnesses and conducted ballistic and medical forensic examinations.
The relatives of the victims or the victims themselves were granted the status of victims in the proceedings of criminal cases nos. 668459 and 67611.
The prosecution was unable to establish the persons responsible for the facts at the heart of the investigation in criminal cases nos. 668459 and 67611.
On 20 February 2007 the investigation in criminal cases nos. 668459 and 67611 was suspended.

The investigator held that "in breach of the instruction on the use of special equipment ... No. 865dsp, officers of the Special Forces Unit ... fired twenty-three 23mm gas grenades" during the events of 25 April 2006.
It was impossible to identify the police officers who had fired the fatal shot during the events of 25 April 2006 near Miskindzha.
On an unidentified date the investigation in criminal cases nos. 668459 and 67611 was reopened after being suspended on 20 February 2007.
On 16 January 2010 the investigation in criminal cases nos. 668459 and 67611 was suspended again.

Under section 12 of the Federal Law on Assemblies, Meetings, Demonstrations, Marches and Picketing (no. 54-FZ of 18 August 2004), the municipal authorities also had to ensure, within their competence and jointly with the organisers and the authorised representative of the Ministry of the Interior, that public order and the safety of citizens while holding the event were respected.
